rejected.why: Viewed 2026-07-30. Wrong subject and unusable. Despite the Commons title the frame is a backlit timber lattice grille silhouetted against white glare — roughly 60 per cent of the picture is solid black. There is no door, no passage, nothing a reader could recognise. Replaced by takoradi-elmina-slave-export-gate.webp.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Four schoolgirls in uniform fill the right half of the frame in sharp close-up, faces fully identifiable, one wearing a legible name badge. We do not publish identifiable close-ups of private individuals, and the picture shows almost nothing of the walkway's height in any case.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Not really the beach: the frame is a paved resort terrace with plastic chairs, tables and thatched parasols, palms silhouetted against a completely blown-out white sky, and a thin strip of sand beyond a fence. Replaced by another frame from the same set.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Uninformative: a blank whitewashed wall with one doorway, below flat grey sky, with the lower 40 per cent of the frame plain cobbles. Nothing identifies it as a fort. Replaced by Fort San Sebastian 5.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Correctly captioned but wrong for the page: it is a grey US Navy amphibious ship being moored by Ghanaian personnel, one of whom carries a slung rifle in the foreground, and the men are shown close enough to be recognisable. It represents a naval visit, not the commercial harbour a cruise passenger sees. Replaced by takoradi-port-harbour.webp.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Wrong continent. The Commons title says Sekondi-Takoradi, but the frame shows the container ship MAERSK NIMES with a Dutch-flagged pilot launch, refinery flare stacks and a northern-European city skyline behind — this is Rotterdam/Europoort, not Ghana. A textbook mislabelled file. Replaced by takoradi-port-harbour-2.webp, which genuinely shows Takoradi.

Viewed 2026-07-30. Genuine and correctly captioned, but a near-duplicate of the female-dungeon frame already in the set and less informative — no memorial wreaths, no signage, nothing to distinguish it. Dropped to keep the set within its size limit rather than for any fault.
